Scope

The whole myth as eBL L/1/6 edits it, in two chapters, translated complete:

  • MB – the Middle Babylonian version from Tell el-Amarna (AmaMB1a = BM E29865, AmaMB1b = VAT 1611; 14th c. BCE, a school text of the Egyptian court): 87 eBL labels (1–17, a+1–a+44, b+1–b+26), labelled here MB.1 … MB.b+26. The short version: the gods' banquet, Namtar sent up for Ereškigal's portion, the god who did not rise, Nergal sent down with fourteen demons, posts them at the fourteen gates, seizes Ereškigal by the hair to behead her; she offers him marriage, kingship and the tablet of wisdom; he kisses her and wipes her tears.
  • SB – the Standard Babylonian version (Sultantepe/Ḫuzirina NA, Uruk Hellenistic, Babylon LB): 333 eBL labels (a+1–a+51, b+1–b+50, c+1–c+65, d+1–d+115, e+1–e+51, f+1). The long version: Kakka goes down the stairway of heaven; Ereškigal sends Namtar up; Nergal does not kneel; Ea makes him a throne and gives him the taboos of the netherworld; Nergal (Erra) goes down, keeps the taboos, then breaks the last one; seven days in bed; he escapes up the stairway; Ea disguises him (bald, squinting, lame); Ereškigal's lament and ultimatum ("I will raise the dead"); Namtar searches the gods twice; Nergal goes down again, seizes her, seven more days; Anu's decree: he stays below for ever.

Total: 420 entries. Order in the files: MB first (annotated-MB.rtl.md), then SB (annotated-SB-1.rtl.md a+1–c+65, annotated-SB-2.rtl.md d+1–f+1).

Base text

eBL L/1/6 (ed. T. D. N. Mitto; rev. A. Hätinen, E. Jiménez, G. Rozzi, Z. J. Földi): ../../sources/eBL/Nergal-and-Ereshkigal-MB/reading-edition.md, ../../sources/eBL/Nergal-and-Ereshkigal-SB/reading-edition.md (git-ignored; built-in sources_sync.py rule). Rank 3: MB – Mitto's German (T (de):, printed by ebl_fetch.py since 2026-10-21); SB – Foster / Mitto's English (T:) and Mitto's German (T (de):; the SB was re-fetched 2026-10-22 after ebl_fetch.py learned other languages and the logogram fix – no line changed). Not available here: Ponchia and Luukko 2013 (SAACT 8, the edition eBL builds on), Gurney 1960, Hutter 1985, Dalley 1989, Foster's Before the Muses, Pettinato 2000.

Line numbering

eBL's labels: a+N etc. are counted from the beginning of a preserved stretch (the tablets' gaps make absolute numbers unknowable); the literature (Gurney, Dalley) uses column numbers – a concordance can be added from eBL's notes when needed. MB 1–17 are the Amarna tablet's obverse; a+, b+ its later stretches.

Comparisons (look for; never force – renderings §11)

Gen 28:12, 17 (the stairway of heaven, the messengers going up and down, "the gate of heaven"); Gen 32:27 ("let me go, for the dawn has risen"); Gen 40:1 (the cupbearer and the baker); Gen 18:4 (water for the feet); Esth 3:2, 5:9 (the one who does not kneel / rise); 2 Kgs 4:26 (הֲשָׁלוֹם); Gen 1:27 (zikar u sinniš); 1 Sam 28 and Deut 18:11 (the dead raised); Isa 14:9–15 (the netherworld rising; going down to the pit); Hos 2:4, 18 (the marriage formula); Lev 21:18–20, 2 Kgs 2:23 (the defects); Lev 12, 15 (impurity); Isa 25:8 (tears wiped); 2 Kgs 17:30 (Nergal of Cuthah); Song 8:6, Ps 139:8.
The ancient mind: hospitality and its taboos (do not eat the food of the dead – cf. Persephone); the court etiquette of the gods (rising before an envoy); a goddess who never knew "the play of maidens"; desire as the force that binds a god to death; kingship of the dead by marriage; the pantheon's politics (Anu, Enlil, Ea; Ea's tricks); the demons of disease as a god's retinue; Amarna as a school text in Egypt.

Open decisions

(numbered; the translators add)

  1. Kakka's name across corpora (SB a+1 …): renderings §11.2 fixed כַּכָּה ★ (vocalized always; since the 2026-10-23 harmonization כַּכָּא, in Enūma eliš too); the Enūma eliš translation has the same god, with the same eBL normalization kaka, as גַּגָּא (EE III 2, 3, 67 – the old reading Gaga). The lead should harmonize (EE III 69–70 are the very formula of SB a+23–a+24).
  2. arkāt simmilat šamāmī (a+11, a+48; later d+26, d+73, d+102, e+19): eBL now reads arkāt as the plural noun ariktu "length(s)" ("all along the stairway of heaven"), not the adjective "long". The fixed formula בְּמַדְרֵגוֹת הַשָּׁמַיִם הָאֲרֻכּוֹת (§11.5, checked by verify) was kept; the apparatus says so. Option: לְאֹרֶךְ מַדְרֵגוֹת הַשָּׁמַיִם.
  3. ellu vs ebbu (a+36, a+41 ilāti ellēti): ellu = טָהוֹר by the precedents (Etana MA h+11, Enūma eliš I 12). Renderings §11.3 gives ebbu (d+67 ul ebbēk) טָהוֹר too – two lemmas, one Hebrew word. Proposal: ebbu = צַח (Gilg. III 99 ebbeti הצחה), or the coordinator moves ellu instead.
  4. mātu "land" = אֶרֶץ (a+38, a+43 ina māti בארץ, Gilgameš X 318, XI 218) while erṣetu = הָאָרֶץ is the netherworld in this text: "Ninurta, the mighty in the land" can be misread as "in the netherworld". Kept the precedent with a note; c+29 / d+94 (ilū ša māti) will meet it again.
  5. Two source words in בָּא: alāku + ventive (a+8, a+30 יבוא; a+34 אשר באת אלינו, after Gilg. IX 49 ša illikannâši הבא אלינו) and erēbu (a+14 בוא, a+22 בא, after Ištar 15, 25). Both precedents kept; the later copies d+24, d+43, d+46 (ša illikannâši) should follow a+34.
  6. ē taʾīr-ma (b+41–b+45; c+56–c+60 ul iʾīram-ma): rendered literally אל תיגש / לא ניגש (âru G "go up to, approach"; e+30 iʾīršī-ma "he went up to her"), against Foster's and Mitto's idiom "take care not to". If the coordinator prefers the idiom, all ten lines change together.
  7. The stative našû in the taboos: נושא לך / נושאים לך for a person (b+40, b+42–b+44), נִשָּׂא לך for the vessel (b+45 mesīt šēpī): one form, two Hebrew forms by subject.
  8. eBL lemma slip (b+20): agâ lemmatized as agû I "crown"; the edition's own note reads a carpentry tool ("axe"): rendered כַּשִּׁיל (not כֶּתֶר, not Jer 10:3's מַעֲצָד).
  9. wadû D "identify" (c+15, c+19): Gilg. XII 14, 34 render it ידע (יֵדְעוּךָ), but the ידע gate of netherworld_tools.py is licensed only by edû / zu and does not accept wadû; rendered הִכִּיר (יכירנו, אכירנו). Option: add wadû / uʾaddû to the gate and use ידע as XII.
  10. ṭeḫû "approach" (d+30 iṭeḫḫâm-ma?): הִתְקָרֵב, to keep it apart from âru = ניגש (b+41, ruling 6) inside this text; Adapa (ina ṭeḫîšu בגשתו) and Gilg. III 1 (ṭiḫâ גְּשָׁה) render ṭeḫû נגש – a cross-corpus split.
  11. šasû = צָעַק throughout this text (b+37 from Gilg. III 120, d+37, d+48), although Gilg. XI 117 (flood corpus), the source of d+48's kīma ālitti כיולדה, has צווחת.
  12. ilū ša māti (c+29, = d+94) = האלים של ארץ (mātu without the article, ruling 4) – awkward Hebrew; alternative אלי ארץ (החיים).
  13. c+51 (umma) (UrkHel1 only) left untranslated: it opens the speech, and the opening quotation mark does its work; c+52's umma = לאמור. A departure from the rule that parenthesized normalization words are translated.
  14. šadâšu elû (d+25, d+47) kept literal (הָרוֹ יעלה / הָרוֹ עָלָה), the idiom for "depart" (elsewhere "die"); Foster and Mitto translate the idiom.
  15. The three defects (d+31; d+99, d+101): קֵרֵחַ, פּוֹזֵל, חִגֵּר – the plain words (Mishnaic חִגֵּר), so that neither Lev 21:18 פִּסֵּחַ nor Gen 32:32 צֹלֵעַ is preferred by the Hebrew; both are in the apparatus.
  16. Tenses of the third copy of the bathing scene: c+61–c+62 and d+5–d+6 are past (īrub, iltabbiš באה, לבשה), but c+63 / d+7 keep the present (izzaz, uštabarrâm-ma): עומדת?, את יופיה? מַרְאָה לו – (participles), against Foster's and Mitto's past.
  17. reḫû (d+65 = d+81 urtaḫânni) = נִזְקַק לְ־ (Mishnaic euphemism), to keep it apart from niāku בָּא עַל and nâlu / itūlu שָׁכַב (renderings §11.3); itūlu (littatīl) = שָׁכַב (Gilg. VI 180–181). Option: בָּא אֵלַי.
  18. ašāru "inspect" (d+95–d+96, d+110–d+112) = סָקַר (Enūma eliš VII 122 īšuru ilī šīmāti), not בָּחַן (barû, wisdom corpus) or פָּקַד.
  19. qāta mullû (e+6 qātukka lumalli) rendered by sense בידך אמסור – not מִלֵּא יָד, the false friend recorded for Etana.
  20. nêʾu irta (e+15) "turn back the breast" kept literal with הִטָּה (שׁוּב is târu's, הָפַךְ târu ana's).
  21. ḫamāṣu (e+1) תָּלַשׁ; uprû (e+31) צָנִיף; ṣerretu (e+17) מֵיתָר; talālu (a bow, e+18) דָּרַךְ (Ps 7:13) – new words, no precedent found.
  22. e+22–e+28: the gatekeeper is the object (atâ), with Mitto; nadānu ana + infinitive "allow" = נתן ל־ (Gen 20:6); the verb i-LUL-šu-ma ("hung him"? "struck him"?) left as ….
  23. The fourteen demons (MB.a+26–a+29 → b+3–b+9): transparent names translated as names, without the article – muttabriqu מִתְבָּרֵק (Hitpael for the Gtn "flashing again and again"; barāqu ~ בָּרָק), rābiṣu רוֹבֵץ [cognate], ṭerdu מְגָרֵשׁ (not טֶרֶד, a modern false friend), idiptu נְשִׁיבָה (מַשַּׁב is zaqīqu's), ṣīdānu סְחַרְחֹרֶת, miqtu מַפָּל, Bēl-ūri בַּעַל־הַגַּג, ummu חֹם (not קַדַּחַת, the word of Deut 28:22), ḫurbāšu צְמַרְמֹרֶת; opaque ones transliterated: šarabdû שַׁרַבְּדּוּ, bennu בֶּנּוּ, liʾbu לִיבּוּ. רֶשֶׁף, דֶּבֶר, קֶטֶב, שֵׁד are kept out of the > lines (apparatus only: Hab 3:5, Deut 32:24, Ps 91:6).
  24. dabābu (MB.a+6–a+7) = סִפֵּר (Gilg. X 250, Etana II 47), so that דִּבֵּר stays with zakāru; "מספרים עמו" is slightly unusual Hebrew.
  25. tarbaṣu (MB.b+10) = מַרְבֵּץ [cognate] (Etana III 33), kept apart from kisallu חָצֵר; the root is that of rābiṣu רוֹבֵץ at the fifth gate.
  26. qadādu D (MB.b+15) = הִרְכִּין (Hebrew has no causative of קדד; the cognate in the apparatus, Gen 24:26).
  27. kurummatu (MB.4) = מָנָה (Gilg. VI 26, XI 221–225) and manû "count" (MB.a+8, a+10, a+13) = מָנָה [cognate] – a Hebrew homograph of two Akkadian words (noun / verb), both by precedent or cognate; מְנֵה and מָנָה are vocalized where the verb is meant. zittu (MB.a+42) = חֵלֶק.
  28. ibakki uddaḫḫas (MB.13 = b+19) = בוכה, מתענה – unvocalized, the same for either gender, as the subject of MB.13 is uncertain.
  29. āmeru (MB.a+24 "the 7 and 7") = רוֹאִים (the participle of amāru, kept), against Mitto's "Wächter".

Ereškigal's message d+62–d+72 (= d+78–d+88): לאמור: 'מאז קטנה הייתי, ובת הייתי, / לא ידעתי את מחול העלמות, / לא ידעתי את דילוג הקטנות. / האל ההוא אשר שלחתם אלינו? – נזקק לי?; ישכב? עמי! / את האל ההוא שִׁלְחוּ אלינו?, ויהי חֲתָנִי, ילין עמי! / טמאה אני – ולא צחה? לא אָדוּן את דין האלים הגדולים, / האלים הגדולים היושבים בקרב אירכלה? / אם את האל ההוא לא תשלחו, / כפולחני אירכלה והארץ הגדולה, / אעלה את המתים, ויאכלו את החיים, / על החיים ארבה את המתים!'". (§11.3); šarrūta ina erṣeti rapašti מלכות בארץ הרחבה (SB c+36); ṭuppu ša nēmeqi לוּחַ הַחָכְמָה; iṣbassī-ma אחז אותה (SB e+31), unaššaqši נישק אותה (našāqu נָשַׁק), dimtaša ikappar את דמעתה מחה (kapāru מָחָה, §11.3; dimtu דִּמְעָה).

XII 14); karāru הֵנִיחַ; ṣeḫru קָטָן; duḫḫusu Dt הִתְעַנָּה; ali אַיֵּה; ša ina pānīya lā itbû אשר לפניי לא קם (MB.a+4, a+8, a+11, a+15, a+39); dabābu סִפֵּר; manû מָנָה; arkû אַחֲרוֹן; gubbuḫu קֵרֵחַ; yānu אֵינֶנּוּ; kabtu כָּבֵד; balāṭu D הֶחֱיָה; palāḫu פָּחַד (Gilg. V 97); āmeru רוֹאֶה; alāku Š הוֹלִיךְ; the demons (decision 23); uppu מַנְעוּל; ramû D הִרְפָּה, G רָפָה (ורפו ידיו, 2 Sam 4:1); šaprāku שָׁלוּחַ אני; ina pī bābi בפתח השער; barû בָּחַן; lasāmu רָץ; ḫalāqu אָבַד; zittu חֵלֶק; tarbaṣu מַרְבֵּץ; ṣābu צָבָא; petû D (stative) פָּתוּחַ לִרְוָחָה; anumma הִנֵּה; qadādu D הִרְכִּין; ṣabātu Š הֶאֱחִיז; nēmequ חָכְמָה; kapāru מָחָה; adu kīnanna עַד כֹּה.

MB ↔ SB: the strongest differences (for the apparatus and the introduction).

  1. The offence: MB – the god did not rise (lā itbû, a+4 …) when the gods rose for Namtar (MB.7); SB – the gods knelt (kamsū, b+4, c+28) and he did not kneel (b+8) – or, in Namtar's report, "stood" (c+30). The two versions split Esth 5:9 (וְלֹא קָם) and 3:2 (לֹא יִכְרַע) between them.
  2. The road: MB has no stairway, no seven gates, no gate names; SB has מדרגות השמים הארוכות six times and seven named gatekeepers. MB has fourteen gates and fourteen disease demons, posted by Nergal as a conqueror; SB has Nergal pass the gates alone and humbly.
  3. Ea's help: MB – a bare chair and fourteen demons; SB – a throne of three woods painted as silver, lapis and gold (Jer 10:3–4), and the taboos of the netherworld (no MB counterpart: [absent]).
  4. The disguise: MB – a bald god "at the back" (a+10); SB – bald, squinting and lame, by Ea's sprinkled water (d+31).
  5. Ereškigal: MB – a sister who wants the offender dead (a+5, a+40) and pleads for her life (b+17); SB – a daughter of Anu who never knew "the dance of maidens", is impure after seven days, laments "the bridegroom of my delight", and threatens to raise the dead.
  6. The union: MB – seizure by the hair to behead her, then a marriage contract (אַתָּה הֱיֵה בַעְלִי…, kingship, the tablet of wisdom), a kiss and wiped tears (Isa 25:8); SB – desire, the broken taboo, two "weeks" in bed (Gen 29:27), flight "before daybreak" (Gen 32:27), and Anu's decree "for days of eternity".
  7. Namtar: MB – killed ("cut down") in the courtyard (b+10); SB – the go-between who climbs the stairway three times and fails to recognize the god.
  8. The setting: MB – a school text of the Egyptian court (dots for word division, perhaps the teacher's "up to here" in b+26); SB – a library text of Assyria and Babylonia that quotes Gilgameš (X 92–94, III 120, VII 184–190, XI 309) and Enūma eliš (III 69–70).
